change.title: pr-67876-flat
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: OAuth `state` is a constant, not a per-session secret
findings.body:
`pipeline.signature` is `md5_text(*pipe_ids)` over the view class names (src/sentry/pipeline/base.py:132-133). It is the same value for every user and every session; the tests hardcode it as `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`. The check at line 412 therefore cannot tie the GitHub callback to the browser session that started the flow.

Here is the attack: an attacker gets a fresh `code` for their own GitHub account. They then get a victim who is partway through the pipeline to load `/extensions/github/setup/?code=<attacker code>&state=9cae5e88…`. The victim's pipeline then binds `github_authenticated_user` to the attacker's login. That defeats the sender check at lines 501-505, which this PR adds as its security control.

The existing `OAuth2LoginView` does this correctly: it generates `secrets.token_hex()`, stores it with `pipeline.bind_state("state", state)` and compares it with `pipeline.fetch_state("state")` (src/sentry/identity/oauth2.py:245-252, 318-325). Do the same here, and update the tests so they read the state from the redirect instead of hardcoding it.

findings.title: `integration.metadata["sender"]` raises KeyError when an Integration has no sender
findings.body:
`sender` is only added to metadata when the install came through the webhook (`build_integration` lines 376-377, webhook.py:202-210). Integrations created by the in-Sentry pipeline have no `sender`; `test_basic_flow` asserts the metadata without one (tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:303-310). Integrations created before `sender` was recorded don't have one either. The sibling endpoint guards for this case with `if "sender" not in integration.metadata` (src/sentry/integrations/github/installation.py:44).

If such an Integration still exists without an OrganizationIntegration, reaching this line raises KeyError, so the user gets a 500 in the popup instead of the error page. The test that re-installs after removing the OrganizationIntegration avoids this only by also deleting the Integration (test_integration.py:360-365).

Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and send the missing case to `error(...)`, or decide on and document a behaviour for legacy integrations.

findings.title: Network or HTTP failures in the token exchange and user lookup become 500s
findings.body:
Two calls can raise uncaught:
- `safe_urlopen(...)` runs outside the `try` that starts at line 425, so a connection error or timeout reaching GitHub is not handled.
- `get_user_info` calls `resp.raise_for_status()` (src/sentry/identity/github/provider.py:16). A 401 or 5xx from `api.github.com/user` raises `HTTPError` at line 434.

In both cases the popup shows a server error and never posts `{"success": false}` to `window.opener` the way `error()` does, so the opener gets no failure result. Put both calls inside the try and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure.

findings.title: Authorize URL query string is built without encoding
findings.body: `client_id`, `state` and `redirect_uri` are put into the URL as raw text. `redirect_uri` is an absolute URL, so a query string or special characters in it would corrupt the authorize request. The sibling `OAuth2LoginView` builds the URL with `urlencode(params)` (src/sentry/identity/oauth2.py:250). Doing the same here only changes the exact-string assertion at test_integration.py:233-236.

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` no longer tests a missing installation
findings.body:
The test now sends `state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`, which is not the pipeline signature. The request therefore stops at the state check (integration.py:412-413), and the test asserts the generic "Invalid installation request." message. The 404 stub at lines 381-383 is never reached, and the `build_integration` path that raises "The GitHub installation could not be found." (integration.py:354-356) is now untested.

Complete the OAuth step with the valid state, then send the `installation_id`, and assert the original not-found message again.

contracts.action: OAuthLoginView redirects to GitHub authorize with state=pipeline.signature
contracts.before_after: The sibling creates a random state with secrets.token_hex(), binds it to pipeline state and urlencodes the params. The new view uses the constant pipeline signature, binds nothing and does not encode the params.
contracts.visible_effect: The user is sent to GitHub to authorize, then back to /extensions/github/setup/ with code and state.
contracts.failure_mode: The state can be predicted, so a forged callback carrying an attacker's code is accepted (see finding).

contracts.action: Token exchange via safe_urlopen and user lookup via get_user_info
contracts.before_after: Only the response read and parse are inside the try. The urlopen call and get_user_info are not.
contracts.visible_effect: On success, github_authenticated_user is bound and the pipeline moves on to GitHubInstallation.
contracts.failure_mode: A network error or a non-2xx response from /user raises, the popup shows a 500 and the opener gets no message.

contracts.action: GitHubInstallation compares the authenticated user with integration.metadata sender
contracts.before_after: The sibling checks `"sender" not in integration.metadata` before reading it. The new code indexes it directly.
contracts.visible_effect: On a mismatch the user sees the failed-installation page and the opener receives success:false.
contracts.failure_mode: KeyError (500) for an Integration that has no sender.

contracts.action: pipeline_advancer forwards a GitHub install that has no pipeline to the org picker
contracts.before_after: Same behaviour; the list membership check is replaced with an equality check.

summary: The PR adds a GitHub OAuth step before installation so it can check that the Sentry user is the GitHub user who installed the app. The OAuth `state` is the constant pipeline signature, so it gives no CSRF protection, and a forged callback can bind an attacker's login and get past the new sender check. Three more problems need fixing: the sender lookup raises KeyError for integrations that have no `sender`; network or HTTP failures in the token exchange and user lookup cause 500s; and `test_installation_not_found` now only exercises the state mismatch, so the not-found path is untested. The URL-encoding of the authorize query is optional. The `pipeline_advancer` change is a refactor that keeps the same behaviour.
